clue.text: Stroke of bad luck upsetting mechanics

indicators.note: upsetting the word mechanics throws its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Garage staff causing trouble count as a piece of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges the nine letters of MECHANICS.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischance is an unlucky accident, a misfortune striking by chance.

clue.text: I said as I approached, here's leaders prophet

indicators.note: the leaders of the six words before it are their opening letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: Someone recalls what they said as they drew near a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first letter of each of I, said, as, I, approached, here's.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is one of the major Old Testament prophets.

clue.text: Small creature found by rotter in American intelligence unit

indicators.note: in places the rotter inside the letters of the intelligence agency

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency of the USA
a cad is a rotter, an ungentlemanly man

explanation.surface: A tiny animal is discovered beside a scoundrel within a US spy agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is a small insect known for its loud shrill song.

clue.text: A cheap alternative for the lawless hooligan

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters of a cheap gives a new word

explanation.surface: A low-cost substitute is offered for a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges A CHEAP. The definition uses the old sense of a Parisian street ruffian.
explanation.definitionFit: An apache was a violent Parisian street gangster of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Smart country boy and girl tucking into a dish

indicators.note: tucking into means the boy and girl are placed inside the other pair of words

parts.note: chic means smart, stylish
a land is a country
Ken is a boy's name
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A stylish rural lad and lass sit down to eat a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart country' reads as a rural fashion plate, but the boy and girl are tucked inside the split smart-plus-country pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken Maryland is fried chicken served with banana and corn fritters, a classic dish.

clue.text: Later Bill got one alternative

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck on a wall
I is the Roman numeral one
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill later picked another option.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterior means coming after in time, subsequent.

clue.text: Britain has an unruly symbol

indicators.note: unruly letters are disorderly, so Britain and an are rearranged

explanation.surface: The nation is said to possess a disorderly emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia, the helmeted female figure with trident, personifies Britain as its emblem.

clue.text: Salt from the shop pa exchanged

indicators.note: the letters of the shop pa are exchanged among themselves into a new order

explanation.surface: Father swapped some table salt bought at the store.
explanation.definitionFit: A phosphate is a salt of phosphoric acid in chemistry.

clue.text: Quarter day?

definitions.meaning: a quarter is one of four equal parts
a day of the month, as in the US holiday on the ... of July

explanation.definitionFit: A quarter is one part in four, and a date can be named by its number in the month.

clue.text: Cash in car had been exchanged for something very sweet

indicators.note: the letters of cash in car had been exchanged around, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Money left in a vehicle was swapped for a sugary treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had been exchanged' rearranges CASH IN CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharin is an artificial sweetener hundreds of times sweeter than sugar.

clue.text: Symbol of one's social position

parts.note: the first word of that phrase also means social position

explanation.definitionFit: Status means standing or rank in society, the thing a status symbol displays.

clue.text: Welcome sign of nervousness

definitions.meaning: a greeting gesture of clasped palms
a trembling of the fingers when anxious

explanation.definitionFit: Clasping palms greets a visitor, while a trembling paw betrays anxiety.

clue.text: Chew noisily during a crisis

explanation.definitionFit: To munch audibly, or a critical moment, as in the idiom when it comes to the crunch.

clue.text: Bobby reads the list

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or read carefully
a table is a list of figures or data

explanation.surface: A policeman goes through the register.
explanation.walkthrough: BOBBY is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank, nicknamed a bobby after Robert Peel.

clue.text: Baseball player doesn't have much of break

parts.note: to be short is to lack enough of something
a stop is a break or pause

explanation.surface: A ballplayer is short of time for a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortstop is the fielder stationed between second and third base.

clue.text: Frosts, say, coming before second half of winter, according to would-be poet

indicators.note: coming before places the first piece ahead of the next
say signals that the word for frosts is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: rimes are hoar frosts

indicators.note: the second half of winter is its last three letters

explanation.surface: Wintry weather inspires a hopeful versifier, perhaps Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Frost was a poet, so 'Frosts, say' pretends to mean poets; really rimes are frosts, spoken to give their soundalike. Only the last three letters of winter are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of trivial verse, a poetaster.

clue.text: Trust worker

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Trust worker (3)', gives ANT only from 'worker'; 'Trust' has no job and is likely an OCR misreading not recoverable without the scan.

clue.text: A couple of new drivers had the lot

indicators.note: a couple of means two copies of the learner letter

parts.note: L is the learner plate shown by new drivers in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: All means everything, the whole amount.

clue.text: Best quality surface

explanation.definitionFit: Finest grade, or the uppermost side of an object.

clue.text: Examiner of pupils whether they are at school or not

definitions.text: Examiner of pupils whether they are at school or not

parts.words: Examiner of pupils whether they are at school or not
parts.note: pupils here are parts of the eye, not schoolchildren, so the examiner is an eye doctor

explanation.definitionFit: An eye specialist inspects the pupils of eyes belonging to anyone, scholar or not.

clue.text: Where Tom may sit and sup

definitions.meaning: a tom is a male cat, which sits on one's thighs
to drink with the tongue like a cat

explanation.definitionFit: A seated person's thighs form a seat for a cat, and cats drink by lapping.

clue.text: Be sparing with money initially in the bag

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for a bag

parts.note: a scrip is an old word for a small bag or wallet

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word money

explanation.surface: Someone is careful with cash, starting with what's in their purse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes M from money; 'in' puts it inside SCRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise, spending as little as possible.

clue.text: His attack might be foiled

parts.note: foiled means parried by a foil, the sword used in a fencing bout

explanation.definitionFit: A swordsman's thrust can be parried with a foil, the blunted fencing sword.

clue.text: One allowed marine into the band

indicators.note: into places the marine inside the other two pieces

parts.note: a is one
let means allowed
RM stands for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A single permitted sailor joins the group.
explanation.walkthrough: RM, short for Royal Marine, is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band worn round the upper arm.

clue.text: Favour the shed

definitions.meaning: a small hut built against a wall

explanation.definitionFit: To incline towards something, or a sloping-roofed hut built against a wall.

clue.text: How students succeed — gradually

definitions.meaning: students succeed by earning university qualifications

explanation.definitionFit: Graduates succeed through university awards; the phrase also means step by step.

clue.text: Help donkey, it's in trouble

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of it's are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone urges aid for a donkey that is in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to aid or support.

clue.text: Man is clue perhaps, male is the answer

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of man is clue may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a man suggests the solution is male.
explanation.definitionFit: Masculine means having qualities of a man.

clue.text: Name of two individuals in the fifties

indicators.note: in places the two individuals between the fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties give two of that letter
I is the Roman numeral one, an individual
one is an individual, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A name belongs to two people in their fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two individuals' gives I and ONE; 'in' puts them between two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel is a man's first name.

clue.text: A duke has the address, love

parts.note: an oration is a formal address or speech

explanation.surface: A nobleman delivers a speech, my dear.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship.
